name: retro-tv
title: Retro TV
description: A 1980s tube TV in perspective, as a dashboard widget: any children render on its screen in green, amber or white phosphor, behind curved glass with scanlines, a vignette, a flickering glare and glow, in a wood cabinet with knobs, a speaker grille, an LED and a power button (UI SDK's toggle). Switching off collapses the picture to a line, then to a dot that fades; TvPowerOff plays it over the whole page, for logging out.

docs: `<RetroTv label power|defaultPower onPowerChange phosphor perspective disabled labels>` with the screen's content as children. The screen is a 4:3 box that children fill (`h-full`), sized by `--retro-tv-screen-width` and `--retro-tv-screen-height`, lengths in pixels for a grid such as 40 × 25 teletext cells, and a size container (`cqw`, `cqh`). Inside it the theme's tokens become phosphor (`foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `card`, `border`, `primary`, `chart-1` to `chart-5`, the series), so stat cards and charts render in it unchanged; add your own padding. The power button is UI SDK's Toggle (`labels.power`, "Power" by default) and `onPowerChange(power, details)` gets its details: `details.cancel()` keeps the set as it is. Switching off collapses the picture to a line, then to a dot that fades, and switching on plays it back; under reduced motion it fades. While off, the screen is `inert`. Agents call `powerOn` and `powerOff`. `useTvPowerOff({ phosphor })` gives `{ overlay, powerOff, reset, playing }`: render `overlay` once, and `await powerOff()` before navigating, as on "log out"; `TvPowerOff playing` is the overlay alone. The cabinet and screen are a fixed palette in every theme (the item's `css`).
